interest: This file is valuable to historians of the Indonesian National Revolution and post-World War II Southeast Asia as it captures contemporary Dutch and Allied intelligence perspectives on Japanese clandestine complicity in the Indonesian independence struggle. It provides concrete details on covert networks such as the 'Black Fan' and 'Day Sang Ka' and identifies key Japanese personnel—including Hitoshi Shimizu, Vice-Admiral Maeda's secretary Saito, Tomegoro Yoshizumi, and Shigetada Nishijima—who facilitated the transfer of arms, military training, and anti-European propaganda to Indonesian nationalists. Furthermore, it records the notable contemporary slogan attributed to Japanese political police officers that 'Japan has been militarily defeated, but is politically victorious,' illustrating how wartime Japanese Pan-Asianist objectives persisted to disrupt European colonial restoration.
overview: This file comprises U.S. State Department Despatch No. 707 dated March 14, 1946, from Counselor of Embassy J. Webb Benton at the American Embassy in The Hague to the Secretary of State, transmitting a copy of an Anep-Aneta news agency bulletin article datelined Batavia, March 5, 1946, entitled 'Japanese Secret Activity.' The enclosed report details widespread post-surrender clandestine and overt collaboration between Japanese military personnel and Indonesian nationalists across Java. It highlights the covert distribution of Japanese weapons and ammunition in Surabaya and elsewhere, the subversive propaganda and intelligence operations of Japanese-sponsored organizations such as the 'Black Fan' and 'Day Sang Ka,' and the role of Japanese officers serving as advisers and instructors to Indonesian nationalist forces in Bandung, Malang, Jogjakarta, and Tjikampek under the operative ethos that Japan, though militarily defeated, was politically victorious.

subfiles.about: Transmittal of a Netherlands News Agency press report on clandestine Japanese activities and collaboration with Indonesian nationalists in Java.
subfiles.from: J. Webb Benton, Counselor of Embassy (for the Ambassador)
subfiles.summary: J. Webb Benton, Counselor of Embassy at the American Embassy in The Hague, transmits to the Secretary of State Despatch No. 707 enclosing an article titled 'Japanese Secret Activity' datelined Batavia, March 5, 1946, from the Netherlands News Agency's 'Anep-Aneta Bulletin.' Benton highlights a statement by an officer of the Japanese Political Police boasting that 'Japan has been militarily defeated but is politically victorious.' The despatch was forwarded via air pouch unrestricted for the attention of the Department.

subfiles.about: News report detailing Japanese underground operations, weapons distribution, clandestine organizations, and military instruction supporting Indonesian nationalists in Java.
subfiles.summary: The report from an Aneta correspondent describes covert Japanese initiatives in Java commencing immediately after Japan's capitulation, including Hitoshi Shimizu's terrorist organization 'Black Fan' and widespread distribution of weapons and ammunition from police stations and military depots to Indonesian nationalists, as corroborated by Colonel Huyer in Surabaya. It reveals the operations of 'Day Sang Ka,' a clandestine organization led by Saito, Yoshizumi, and Nishizima that trained Indonesian youths in intelligence, anti-European agitation, and terrorism. The article further reports ongoing open military collaboration, with Japanese officers acting as advisers, instructors, and commanders for Indonesian forces and air-training centers in Bandung, Malang, Jogjakarta, and Tjikampek to ensure post-war political victory.
subfiles.title: Article 'Japanese Secret Activity' from Anep-Aneta Bulletin
